title: U5 - Review findings
outcome: The four findings from the review of PRJ-0000 are closed. The published image carries no front-end toolchain under /workspace, so the reversibility condition that the image gains no node dependency for the product is true rather than intended. The provider command-line tools under /usr/local/lib legitimately ship node and their own modules, and are untouched. Every one of the thirteen domain capabilities is either assigned or recorded as deliberately unowned with a reason, so a gap is a decision rather than an oversight. Running the product does not modify configuration files that are under version control, so development and testing stop dirtying the tree. A loopback console session with no locally stored identity resolves to a real registered actor rather than an anonymous one that matches nobody and holds no capabilities, so opening the console for the first time is never a dead end with no way to reach Settings.
notInScope: No new product capability, no interface redesign, no change to the vocabulary or the information architecture settled in MS-0008 and MS-0010. No change to the build toolchain itself: the three pinned packages, the committed page and the drift gate all stand. This milestone closes findings, and a finding that turns out to need design is raised rather than absorbed here. No login screen or identity-picker UI, and no change to oidc-required behaviour: the fix stays inside the development-local loopback trust boundary that already exists.
completionEvidence: The image is rebuilt and inspected: no /workspace/node_modules, no /workspace front-end source directory, with the provider tooling under /usr/local/lib intact, and the size difference from before is recorded in the pull request. A test fails if a future image would carry them. Every capability resolves to an owner or to a recorded decision, asserted by a test rather than by reading the file. Running the server against a clean checkout leaves `git status` clean, demonstrated by starting it, exercising it and showing no modification. Starting the server against a clean checkout, calling /api/auth/whoami with no identity headers -- exactly what a browser with an empty profile sends -- returns an actor that can reach Settings -> Users or is otherwise handed a real identity, demonstrated against the running server rather than inferred from a capability count.

metadata.origin: Findings from the review of PRJ-0000 on 2026-08-20. PRJ-0000 returns to ACTIVE because a project whose review found an unmet reversibility condition is not finished; COMPLETE would say the tasks were closed, which was true, and would imply the outcome held, which was not.
metadata.risk: The image finding is the only one with a shipped consequence to a security review; the loopback-identity finding is the only one that stops the product from being used at all -- a fresh install's first screen is a dead end, and the message on it names a role ("an organization owner or admin") the caller has no way to become. The temptation is to treat a 200 response as the bar and call the console working. Both of those are the ones that must not be deferred; the other two are hygiene.
metadata.estimateDelta: 0.5 -> 0.85 fpd (+0.35), high-end stance: the identity-resolution finding sits in the security-sensitive-implementation band (PW-EST), not the hygiene band the first three findings were budgeted at, and is printed here rather than folded into the existing figure.
